g.text: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged
as a powerful paradigm for training large language models to
perform complex reasoning (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Shao et al.,
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=2) Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for training large language models to perform complex reasoning (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025; Shao et al., 2024).

g.text: By providing binary correctness signals from programmatic verifiers, RLVR
enables models to develop sophisticated chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning
capabilities without requiring dense human feedback.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) By providing binary correctness signals from programmatic verifiers, RLVR enables models to develop sophisticated chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning capabilities without requiring dense human feedback.

g.text: Recent systems such as DeepSeek-R1 demonstrate that RLVR can produce
reasoning traces spanning thousands of tokens, enabling multi-step problem
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) Recent systems such as DeepSeek-R1 demonstrate that RLVR can produce reasoning traces spanning thousands of tokens, enabling multi-step problem solving on challenging mathematical benchmarks.

g.text: However, long-horizon reasoning introduces a fundamental challenge:
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) However, long-horizon reasoning introduces a fundamental challenge: truncation.

g.text: Due to computational constraints, training rollouts must be capped at a
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=0) Due to computational constraints, training rollouts must be capped at a maximum token length Lmax.

g.text: When a model's reasoning exceeds this limit without reaching a conclusion,
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=0) When a model's reasoning exceeds this limit without reaching a conclusion, the trajectory is truncated mid-thought.

g.text: The standard approach treats such truncations as failures,
assigning a reward of −1 (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025).
g.title: N7 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) The standard approach treats such truncations as failures, assigning a reward of −1 (DeepSeek-AI et al., 2025).

g.text: This conflates unfinished reasoning with incorrect reasoning,
potentially biasing training against the extended deliberation
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) This conflates unfinished reasoning with incorrect reasoning, potentially biasing training against the extended deliberation needed for difficult problems.

g.text: We propose timeout bootstrapping, drawing from classical RL theory
g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=1) We propose timeout bootstrapping, drawing from classical RL theory on time limits (Pardo et al., 2017).

g.text: The key insight is that truncation due to token limits is an artificial
timeout, not a terminal state indicating failure.
g.title: N12 [Method] (cites=0) The key insight is that truncation due to token limits is an artificial timeout, not a terminal state indicating failure.

the critic's value estimate at truncation, treating the partial trajectory
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=0) For tasks without inherent time constraints, the agent should bootstrap from the critic's value estimate at truncation, treating the partial trajectory as ongoing rather than failed.

g.text: Effective in control, untested in LMs
This approach has proven effective in continuous control domains
but has not been systematically evaluated for language model
g.title: N14 [Context] (cites=0) This approach has proven effective in continuous control domains but has not been systematically evaluated for language model reasoning.

g.text: We conduct a pre-registered empirical comparison of three
truncate-as-failure, DAPO overlong shaping, and timeout
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) We conduct a pre-registered empirical comparison of three truncation strategies on mathematical reasoning: truncate-as-failure, DAPO overlong shaping, and timeout bootstrapping.

g.text: Promising but fails criteria; critic collapse
Our experiments reveal that while timeout bootstrapping shows promise on
stable training runs (+2.20pp over baseline on the long subset), it fails
our pre-registered success criteria on average due to a critical failure
g.title: N16 [Result] (cites=0) Our experiments reveal that while timeout bootstrapping shows promise on stable training runs (+2.20pp over baseline on the long subset), it fails our pre-registered success criteria on average due to a critical failure mode: the critic's value estimates collapse to −1.0 within the first 15–20 training steps, rendering bootstrapping equivalent to truncate-as-failure.

g.text: Further analysis reveals that the critic exhibits negative correlation with
g.title: N17 [Result] (cites=0) Further analysis reveals that the critic exhibits negative correlation with final correctness (Pearson r = −0.211, AUROC = 0.314), indicating fundamental miscalibration on reasoning prefixes.

g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We formalize three truncation handling strategies for RLVR and provide the first systematic comparison on long-horizon mathematical reasoning.
